tools.name: analyze_har
tools.description: Run every analysis over a .har file and return a triage overview: blast radius, finding counts, and a one-line verdict per check. Start here — then use the focused tools for detail.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

tools.name: har_brief
tools.description: The complete audit as markdown, with every secret masked and the analysis's own blind spots stated. This is the safe artifact to quote, paste into a ticket, or reason over.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

tools.name: har_findings
tools.description: Findings raised against the capture — leaked tokens, PII in URLs, insecure cookies, missing headers, expired tokens. Details are redacted.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

severity.description: Only findings at this severity. Omit for all.

tools.name: har_vendors
tools.description: Every third party the capture contacted, scored 0–100 by how much damage it could do: request volume, bytes, cookies set, and credentials or PII observed reaching it.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

tools.name: har_csp
tools.description: Synthesize a starter CSP from what this capture actually loaded, diffed against the policy the origin sends today.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

tools.name: har_hunt
tools.description: Search the capture with the Hunt query language. Supports free text plus filters like `is:thirdparty`, `status:404`, `type:script`, `host:example.com`, `method:POST`.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.

tools.name: sanitize_har
tools.description: Mask secrets, tokens, emails, card numbers, and response bodies, then write a `.redacted.har` next to the original. Run this before attaching a capture to a ticket — enterprise DLP now blocks unsanitized HAR uploads outright.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .har file on this machine.
